# Minimal Surface Convention

Every field you copy and every parameter you accept is something a future reader has to check for meaning. A hand-rolled mapping that changes nothing invites the question *what is different here* and answers it with nothing; a parameter nobody reads has to be kept working forever by people who cannot tell it is dead. Both are surface that was never asked for.

## Scope

Applies to every hand-written `.ts` / `.tsx` / `.js` source file.

Does **not** apply to generated output (codegen, tool-emitted `*.d.ts`, build directories), database migrations, or third-party shims copied verbatim.

## Return the object you already have

When the value already matches the return type structurally, return it as-is — do not rebuild it field by field. Map only when a field genuinely needs renaming or converting (`String(amount)`, `email ?? null`).

```ts
// CORRECT — shape already matches AccessToken
return node ?? null;

// WRONG — manual mapping that changes nothing
return node ? { title: node.title, accessToken: node.accessToken } : null;
```

The rebuilt version also silently drops any field added upstream later, which is a bug that looks like nothing at the site that causes it.

## No speculative parameters

Do not pass, accept, or keep a parameter, field, or overload that no consumer reads. When a refactor exposes a "just in case" argument — `new UpstreamError(message, userErrors)` while nothing reads `error.userErrors` — drop it at the call site.

One operation gets one fallback message. Do not distinguish `'Failed to create page'` from `'pageCreate failed'` between two error shapes: the two wordings imply a difference the reader then goes looking for, and there is none.

```ts
// WRONG — payload nobody reads, second wording for the same failure
if (userErrors.length > 0) {
  throw new UpstreamError(userErrors[0]?.message ?? 'pageCreate failed', userErrors);
}
```

The correct shape of that read is in [nested-access-convention.md](./nested-access-convention.md); what matters here is the argument that no consumer touches.

"We might need it later" is the reason this surface exists, and later rarely comes. When it does, adding the parameter back is one line — cheaper than every reader who had to work out whether it mattered in the meantime.

## NEVER Do

- Rebuild an object field by field when its shape already matches the return type.
- Pass or keep a parameter, field, or overload that no consumer reads.
- Give one operation two different fallback messages for the same failure.
